3. Definitions and Interpretations

4. Corporate Governance

4.1 The Group is committed to high standards of corporate governance in line with the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance and international principles.

4.2 The Board is responsible for the overall strategic direction, oversight of management, and safeguarding of shareholder interests.

4.3 The Board has established the following committees:

- Audit and Risk Committee
- Finance and Investment Committee
- Remuneration and Nomination Committee
- Health, Safety, and Environment Committee

4.4 Each committee operates under its own terms of reference, approved by the Board and reviewed at least annually.

4.5 The Group Managing Director (GMD) is the Chief Executive Officer and is accountable to the Board for the day-to-day management of the Group.

4.6 All employees are expected to act with integrity, honesty, and in the best interests of the Group at all times.

5. Organizational Structure and Subsidiaries

5.1 The Group operates through a parent company, West African Gateway Ports Ltd., with the following principal subsidiaries and business units:

- Lagos Container Terminal Operations (LCTO)
- Apapa Bulk Cargo Handling Services Ltd.
- Tin Can Island Logistics and Warehousing Ltd.
- West African Gateway Marine Services Ltd.
- Port Support Services (Nigeria) Ltd.

5.2 The Group also holds interests in joint ventures and associated companies, details of which are maintained by the Company Secretary.

5.3 Organisational charts are maintained by Human Resources and are available on the intranet. Departmental heads are responsible for ensuring their teams are aware of reporting lines and functional responsibilities.

5.4 The functional responsibilities of major departments are summarised below:

- Operations: Oversees terminal activities, vessel berthing, cargo handling, and stevedoring.
- Engineering: Maintains equipment, infrastructure, and port assets.
- Commercial: Manages customer relationships, tariffs, and business development.
- Finance: Handles accounting, budgeting, treasury, and financial reporting.
- Human Resources: Manages staff recruitment, training, welfare, and industrial relations.
- HSSE: Enforces health, safety, security, and environmental standards.
- Legal & Compliance: Provides legal advice and ensures regulatory compliance.
- Information Technology: Supports systems, networks, and digital services.

6. Fiscal Year and Reporting Calendar

6.1 The fiscal year of the Group runs from 1 January to 31 December each year. This applies to the parent company and all subsidiaries, unless a subsidiary is required by law or regulation to adopt a different period, in which case the matter shall be referred to the Board.

6.2 The fiscal year end is 31 December. Financial statements are prepared as at that date.

6.3 The budget cycle for each fiscal year commences in September of the preceding year. Departments are required to submit their draft budgets to Finance by the last business day of October.

6.4 The Board approves the annual budget at its December meeting. West African Gateway Ports Ltd. fiscal_year_start 2026-01-01 date. Record status: current.

6.6 All reporting deadlines are stated in Lagos Local Time. Where a deadline falls on a non-business day, the deadline is extended to the next business day.

11.1 Annual leave entitlement is based on the staff member's grade and length of service, as
specified in the Staff Handbook. Annual leave shall be taken within the calendar year in which it
is earned, except where operational requirements prevent this. Carry-over of annual leave to the
following year requires the written approval of the Department Head and the Human Resources
Manager. Carry-over shall not exceed ten working days in any case.

**Section 16 – Travel and Expense Policy**

16.1 This Section governs the reimbursement of business expenses incurred by employees of West African Gateway Ports Ltd. ("the Group") in the performance of their duties. The Policy applies to all employees, including temporary staff and secondees, and covers domestic and international travel, accommodation, meals, transport, and incidental expenses.

16.2 All travel and expense claims shall be submitted on the prescribed Expense Claim Form (ECF) within fourteen (14) calendar days of the date of return from travel, or within fourteen (14) calendar days of the date the expense was incurred for non-travel expenses. Claims submitted after this period shall be subject to the approval of the Chief Financial Officer and may be declined.

**Section 17 – Travel Approval and Booking**

17.1 All travel shall be approved in advance by the employee's Department Head, or by the Managing Director for travel by Department Heads and above. The Travel Request (TR) form shall be submitted at least ten (10) business days before the proposed departure date, except in cases of emergency travel where a shorter period may be approved by the Department Head.

17.2 The Group shall arrange and pay for all approved travel bookings, including flights, rail, and accommodation, through the designated travel agency. Employees shall not make their own bookings unless expressly authorised in writing by the CFO.

(b) International travel (Africa, excluding Nigeria): ₦80,000 per day.

(c) International travel (outside Africa): ₦120,000 per day.

18.2 Allowances are calculated on a pro-rata basis for partial days. A day is counted as a full day where the employee is away from their normal place of work for more than twelve (12) hours. Where the employee is away for less than twelve (12) hours, a half-day allowance shall apply.

18.3 Allowances shall cease where the employee is on leave, or where accommodation is provided by a third party and meals are included.

(a) Domestic: ₦60,000.

(b) International (Africa): ₦150,000.

(c) International (outside Africa): ₦250,000.

18.5 No allowance shall be paid for any period during which the employee is travelling on a Group vessel or is otherwise provided with meals and accommodation by the Group.

**Section 20 – Information Technology**

20.1 The Group provides information technology (IT) resources, including computers, mobile
devices, network access, email, and software applications, to support employees in the
performance of their duties. Use of Group IT resources is a privilege, not a right, and is
subject to the terms of this Policy and all applicable laws.

20.2 Employees shall use IT resources primarily for Group business. Incidental personal use
is permitted where it does not interfere with work, does not consume excessive bandwidth or
storage, and does not violate any other provision of this Policy.

20.3 The following activities are strictly prohibited on Group IT resources:

(a) Accessing, storing, transmitting, or distributing material that is pornographic,
obscene, hateful, or otherwise offensive.

(b) Harassing, threatening, or discriminating against any person.

(c) Attempting to breach, bypass, or circumvent any security control, firewall, or access
restriction.

(d) Installing unauthorised software, including peer-to-peer file sharing applications.

(e) Connecting personal devices to the Group network without prior approval from the IT
Department.

(f) Using Group IT resources for any illegal activity, including copyright infringement or
fraud.

20.4 Employees shall not use Group email or messaging systems to send unsolicited bulk
messages (spam) or chain letters.

20.5 The Group may monitor use of its IT resources to ensure compliance with this Policy,
to protect the security of its systems, and for other legitimate business purposes. Employees
shall have no expectation of privacy in their use of Group IT resources.

20.6 Employees shall protect their user credentials, including passwords and PINs, and shall
not share them with any other person. Passwords shall be changed at least every ninety (90)
days.

20.7 Employees shall report any suspected security incident, including lost or stolen
devices, suspected malware, or unauthorised access, to the IT Department immediately upon
becoming aware of the incident.

20.8 Software and hardware shall be procured only through the IT Department. Employees
shall not procure IT equipment or software directly from vendors, whether for Group use or
for reimbursement.

**Section 21 – Data Protection**

21.1 The Group is committed to protecting the personal data of its employees, customers,
suppliers, and other individuals. This Section applies to all personal data processed by the
Group, whether in electronic or paper form.

21.2 "Personal data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural
person. "Processing" means any operation performed on personal data, including collection,
recording, organisation, storage, adaptation, retrieval, use, disclosure, and destruction.

21.3 The Group shall process personal data in accordance with the Nigeria Data Protection
Act 2023 and any other applicable data protection legislation.

21.4 The following principles shall be observed in all processing of personal data:

(a) Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency.

(b) Purpose limitation: personal data shall be collected for specified, explicit, and
legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.

(c) Data minimisation: personal data shall be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is
necessary in relation to the purposes for which it is processed.

(d) Accuracy: personal data shall be accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date.

(e) Storage limitation: personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification
of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which it is processed.

(f) Integrity and confidentiality: personal data shall be processed in a manner that ensures
appropriate security.

21.5 Employees shall only access personal data that is necessary for the performance of
their duties. Access to personal data for curiosity or non-work purposes is prohibited.

21.6 Personal data shall not be disclosed to third parties except where the disclosure is
required by law, is necessary for the performance of the employee's duties, or has been
authorised in writing by the Data Protection Officer (DPO).

3. Definitions and Interpretations

In this manual, unless the context otherwise requires:

4. Corporate Governance

4.1 The Group is committed to high standards of corporate governance in line with the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance and international principles.

4.2 The Board is responsible for the overall strategic direction, oversight of management, and safeguarding of shareholder interests.

4.3 The Board has established the following committees:

- Audit and Risk Committee
- Finance and Investment Committee
- Remuneration and Nomination Committee
- Health, Safety, and Environment Committee

4.4 Each committee operates under its own terms of reference, approved by the Board and reviewed at least annually.

4.5 The Group Managing Director (GMD) is the Chief Executive Officer and is accountable to the Board for the day-to-day management of the Group.

4.6 All employees are expected to act with integrity, honesty, and in the best interests of the Group at all times.

5. Organizational Structure and Subsidiaries

5.1 The Group operates through a parent company, West African Gateway Ports Ltd., with the following principal subsidiaries and business units:

- Lagos Container Terminal Operations (LCTO)
- Apapa Bulk Cargo Handling Services Ltd.
- Tin Can Island Logistics and Warehousing Ltd.
- West African Gateway Marine Services Ltd.
- Port Support Services (Nigeria) Ltd.

5.2 The Group also holds interests in joint ventures and associated companies, details of which are maintained by the Company Secretary.

5.3 Organisational charts are maintained by Human Resources and are available on the intranet. Departmental heads are responsible for ensuring their teams are aware of reporting lines and functional responsibilities.

5.4 The functional responsibilities of major departments are summarised below:

- Operations: Oversees terminal activities, vessel berthing, cargo handling, and stevedoring.
- Engineering: Maintains equipment, infrastructure, and port assets.
- Commercial: Manages customer relationships, tariffs, and business development.
- Finance: Handles accounting, budgeting, treasury, and financial reporting.
- Human Resources: Manages staff recruitment, training, welfare, and industrial relations.
- HSSE: Enforces health, safety, security, and environmental standards.
- Legal & Compliance: Provides legal advice and ensures regulatory compliance.
- Information Technology: Supports systems, networks, and digital services.

6. Fiscal Year and Reporting Calendar

6.1 The fiscal year of the Group runs from 1 January to 31 December each year. This applies to the parent company and all subsidiaries, unless a subsidiary is required by law or regulation to adopt a different period, in which case the matter shall be referred to the Board.

6.2 The fiscal year end is 31 December. Financial statements are prepared as at that date.

6.3 The budget cycle for each fiscal year commences in September of the preceding year. Departments are required to submit their draft budgets to Finance by the last business day of October.

6.4 The Board approves the annual budget at its December meeting. West African Gateway Ports Ltd. fiscal_year_start 2026-01-01 date. Record status: current.

6.5 The reporting calendar for the 2026 fiscal year is as follows:

| Activity | Due Date (Business Day) |
|----------|--------------------------|
| Q1 management accounts | Last business day of April |
| Q2 management accounts | Last business day of July |
| Q3 management accounts | Last business day of October |
| Annual statutory audit | Commences first week of February 2027 |
| Annual general meeting | On or before 30 June 2027 |

6.6 All reporting deadlines are stated in Lagos Local Time. Where a deadline falls on a non-business day, the deadline is extended to the next business day.

7. Business Days and Working Hours

7.1 The standard working week is Monday to Friday. Saturday and Sunday are rest days, except for operational staff whose shift patterns may require weekend work.

8.2 Employees who arrive more than 15 minutes after their scheduled start time shall be marked as late. Three late arrivals in any calendar month constitute one day of unauthorised absence.

8.3 Employees who are unable to attend work due to illness must notify their supervisor before 09:00 on the first day of absence. Medical certificates are required for absences exceeding two consecutive days.

8.4 The Group operates a flexi-time arrangement for administrative staff, subject to departmental approval. Under this arrangement:

- a) The core hours are 10:00 to 15:00, during which all flexi-time employees must be present.
- b) Employees may start between 07:30 and 10:00 and finish between 15:00 and 18:00.
- c) Flexi-time employees must complete 8 hours of work per day, excluding lunch.
- d) Flexi-time is not available to operational staff or to staff in customer-facing roles unless approved by the Head of Department.

8.5 Shift handover procedures are as follows:

- a) The outgoing shift shall complete the handover log, noting any pending issues, equipment status, and safety matters.
- b) The incoming shift shall review the handover log and acknowledge receipt by signature.
- c) Handover shall take place at the shift change time, allowing for a 15-minute overlap. The outgoing shift is responsible for briefing the incoming shift on all relevant matters.
- d) Any unresolved issue at handover shall be escalated to the Shift Manager immediately.

9. Corporate Timezone and Deadline Calculation

9.1 West African Gateway Ports Ltd. operates in the corporate_timezone Africa/Lagos. Record status: current. All official times, including meeting schedules, reporting deadlines, and operational timelines, are stated in Africa/Lagos time unless explicitly noted otherwise.

9.2 When a deadline is stated without a timezone, it shall be interpreted as Africa/Lagos time. This applies to internal documents, external correspondence, and contractual commitments.

9.3 For the avoidance of doubt, Africa/Lagos time is UTC+1 throughout the year. The Group does not observe daylight saving time.

9.4 Meeting scheduling and deadline calculations shall follow the rules below:

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| a) | All meeting invitations shall state the time in Africa/Lagos time, with the timezone abbreviation (WAT) included in the invitation header. |
| b) | When participants are in different timezones, the invitation shall also show the equivalent time in each participant's local timezone, clearly labelled. |
| c) | A meeting scheduled for 10:00 WAT shall be deemed to start at 10:00 WAT regardless of the local time of any participant. |
| d) | Deadlines for submissions, approvals, or payments shall be interpreted as the close of business (17:00) on the stated date in Africa/Lagos time, unless a specific time is stated. |
| e) | Where a deadline falls on a non-business day, the deadline is extended to the next business day. Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays observed by the Group. |

9.5 For meetings involving external parties, the meeting organiser shall confirm the timezone interpretation in the meeting invitation and in any pre-meeting correspondence. If a participant is in a timezone ahead of Africa/Lagos (e.g., Asia or Oceania), the meeting time shall be checked to ensure it falls within the participant's reasonable working hours where practicable.

9.6 The following table provides examples of timezone conversions for common counterparty locations, for reference when scheduling meetings:

| London, UK | UTC+0 | 09:00 |

**Section 11 – Leave Policy**

11.1 Annual leave entitlement is based on the staff member's grade and length of service, as
specified in the Staff Handbook. Annual leave shall be taken within the calendar year in which it
is earned, except where operational requirements prevent this. Carry-over of annual leave to the
following year requires the written approval of the Department Head and the Human Resources

require a second medical opinion at its own cost. Staff who are absent on sick leave for more than
five consecutive working days shall be referred to the Group's occupational health provider.

and the Group's Maternity Policy. Paternity leave shall be five working days. Adoption leave shall

to five working days. Compassionate leave for the death of a grandparent, in-law, or other
relative shall be up to two working days. Staff shall notify their Department Head as soon as
reasonably practicable.

11.5 Unpaid leave may be granted at the discretion of the Human Resources Manager for a period not
exceeding thirty calendar days in any calendar year. Unpaid leave shall not be granted for more
than ten consecutive working days without the approval of the Managing Director.

11.6 All leave requests shall be submitted through the HR portal at least five working days before
the intended start date, except in cases of emergency. The line manager shall approve or reject
the request within three working days of submission. A rejected request shall be accompanied by a
reason and a proposed alternative date where possible.

operational staff may be required to work during the shutdown period, and shall be compensated in
accordance with the Collective Bargaining Agreement.

12.4 All budget holders shall submit a quarterly budget performance report to the CFO's office

budget shall be broken down by department, by cost centre, and by quarter.

13.2 The Board shall approve the annual budget, or refer it back to management for revision,
within fifteen working days of submission. Upon approval, the budget shall be circulated to all
Department Heads, and shall become the basis for all expenditure control during the financial year.

13.3 Quarterly budget revisions may be proposed by a Department Head where there is a material
change in operational circumstances. The revision shall be submitted to the CFO's office in the
prescribed format, and shall be approved by the CFO before the start of the quarter to which it
relates.

13.4 The CFO is authorised to approve the quarterly budget for each department within the
framework of the approved annual budget, and to approve virements between cost centres within a
department of up to ten percent of the department's quarterly budget. Virements above ten percent
shall require the approval of the Managing Director.

13.5 All budget approvals, whether annual, quarterly, or revisionary, shall be recorded in the
budget register, shall bear the date of approval, and shall be signed by the approving officer.

**Section 16 – Travel and Expense Policy**

16.1 This Section governs the reimbursement of business expenses incurred by employees of West African Gateway Ports Ltd. ("the Group") in the performance of their duties. The Policy applies to all employees, including temporary staff and secondees, and covers domestic and international travel, accommodation, meals, transport, and incidental expenses.

16.2 All travel and expense claims shall be submitted on the prescribed Expense Claim Form (ECF) within fourteen (14) calendar days of the date of return from travel, or within fourteen (14) calendar days of the date the expense was incurred for non-travel expenses. Claims submitted after this period shall be subject to the approval of the Chief Financial Officer and may be declined.

16.3 The Group's fiscal year runs from 1 January to 31 December. The official time zone for all Group records, including travel itineraries, expense claims, and attendance records, is West Africa Time (WAT, UTC+1). Where an employee travels outside this time zone, all deadlines and business-day calculations shall be based on WAT, unless a specific exception is stated in writing by the Managing Director.

16.4 Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays observed by the Group. A list of approved public holidays for each calendar year is published by the Human Resources Department no later than 30 November of the preceding year.

**Section 17 – Travel Approval and Booking**

17.1 All travel shall be approved in advance by the employee's Department Head, or by the Managing Director for travel by Department Heads and above. The Travel Request (TR) form shall be submitted at least ten (10) business days before the proposed departure date, except in cases of emergency travel where a shorter period may be approved by the Department Head.

17.2 The Group shall arrange and pay for all approved travel bookings, including flights, rail, and accommodation, through the designated travel agency. Employees shall not make their own bookings unless expressly authorised in writing by the CFO.

17.3 Employees are required to use economy class for all flights of less than six (6) hours duration. Business class is permitted for flights of six (6) hours or more, subject to prior approval. First class travel is not permitted under any circumstances.

17.4 Where an employee uses a personal vehicle for approved travel, mileage shall be reimbursed at the rate published in the annual Budget Circular. The current rate is ₦250 per kilometre.

**Section 18 – Allowances**

18.1 The following daily allowances shall apply to approved travel:

(a) Domestic travel (within Nigeria): ₦35,000 per day, covering meals and incidental expenses.

(b) International travel (Africa, excluding Nigeria): ₦80,000 per day.

(c) International travel (outside Africa): ₦120,000 per day.

18.2 Allowances are calculated on a pro-rata basis for partial days. A day is counted as a full day where the employee is away from their normal place of work for more than twelve (12) hours. Where the employee is away for less than twelve (12) hours, a half-day allowance shall apply.

18.3 Allowances shall cease where the employee is on leave, or where accommodation is provided by a third party and meals are included.

18.4 Where accommodation is not pre-booked by the Group, the employee shall be reimbursed for actual reasonable costs up to the following limits per night:

(a) Domestic: ₦60,000.

(b) International (Africa): ₦150,000.

(c) International (outside Africa): ₦250,000.

18.5 No allowance shall be paid for any period during which the employee is travelling on a Group vessel or is otherwise provided with meals and accommodation by the Group.

**Section 19 – Expense Claims and Documentation**

19.1 All expense claims shall be accompanied by original receipts or invoices. Where an original receipt is lost, a certified copy may be accepted at the discretion of the CFO, provided the employee provides a written explanation for the loss.

**Section 20 – Information Technology**

20.1 The Group provides information technology (IT) resources, including computers, mobile
devices, network access, email, and software applications, to support employees in the
performance of their duties. Use of Group IT resources is a privilege, not a right, and is
subject to the terms of this Policy and all applicable laws.

20.2 Employees shall use IT resources primarily for Group business. Incidental personal use
is permitted where it does not interfere with work, does not consume excessive bandwidth or
storage, and does not violate any other provision of this Policy.

20.3 The following activities are strictly prohibited on Group IT resources:

(a) Accessing, storing, transmitting, or distributing material that is pornographic,
obscene, hateful, or otherwise offensive.

(b) Harassing, threatening, or discriminating against any person.

(c) Attempting to breach, bypass, or circumvent any security control, firewall, or access
restriction.

(d) Installing unauthorised software, including peer-to-peer file sharing applications.

(e) Connecting personal devices to the Group network without prior approval from the IT
Department.

(f) Using Group IT resources for any illegal activity, including copyright infringement or
fraud.

20.4 Employees shall not use Group email or messaging systems to send unsolicited bulk
messages (spam) or chain letters.

20.5 The Group may monitor use of its IT resources to ensure compliance with this Policy,
to protect the security of its systems, and for other legitimate business purposes. Employees
shall have no expectation of privacy in their use of Group IT resources.

20.6 Employees shall protect their user credentials, including passwords and PINs, and shall
not share them with any other person. Passwords shall be changed at least every ninety (90)
days.

20.7 Employees shall report any suspected security incident, including lost or stolen
devices, suspected malware, or unauthorised access, to the IT Department immediately upon
becoming aware of the incident.

20.8 Software and hardware shall be procured only through the IT Department. Employees
shall not procure IT equipment or software directly from vendors, whether for Group use or
for reimbursement.

**Section 21 – Data Protection**

21.1 The Group is committed to protecting the personal data of its employees, customers,
suppliers, and other individuals. This Section applies to all personal data processed by the
Group, whether in electronic or paper form.

21.2 "Personal data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural
person. "Processing" means any operation performed on personal data, including collection,
recording, organisation, storage, adaptation, retrieval, use, disclosure, and destruction.

21.3 The Group shall process personal data in accordance with the Nigeria Data Protection
Act 2023 and any other applicable data protection legislation.

21.4 The following principles shall be observed in all processing of personal data:

(a) Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency.

(b) Purpose limitation: personal data shall be collected for specified, explicit, and
legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.

(c) Data minimisation: personal data shall be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is
necessary in relation to the purposes for which it is processed.

(d) Accuracy: personal data shall be accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date.

(e) Storage limitation: personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification
of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which it is processed.

(f) Integrity and confidentiality: personal data shall be processed in a manner that ensures
appropriate security.

21.5 Employees shall only access personal data that is necessary for the performance of
their duties. Access to personal data for curiosity or non-work purposes is prohibited.

21.6 Personal data shall not be disclosed to third parties except where the disclosure is
required by law, is necessary for the performance of the employee's duties, or has been
authorised in writing by the Data Protection Officer (DPO).
